title: Is a product bigger than the numbers multiplied?
description: Two point two five times eight, zero point two five times eight and zero point two five times zero point eight are found by counting the digits after the point, and each product is compared with the numbers multiplied. Keeko doubts that a product is always bigger than both numbers.
teaching_notes: One idea: multiplying by a number below one takes a part of the other number, so the product can be smaller than it. Watch for students who believe that multiplying always makes a number bigger.

source: Find 2.25 × 8, 0.25 × 8 and 0.25 × 0.8, and compare each product with the two numbers multiplied.
video_script.why: The child can multiply decimals by the digit rule and now looks at how a product compares with the numbers multiplied.
video_script.substitution: the book's three products, two point two five times eight, zero point two five times eight, and zero point two five times zero point eight
video_script.anchor: Three products from the book, each to be compared with the two numbers multiplied
video_script.wrong_answer: a product is always bigger than both the numbers multiplied
video_script.wrong_move: A common slip believes that multiplying always makes a bigger number. Zero point two five times eight is two, which is smaller than eight, and zero point two five times zero point eight is zero point two, which is smaller than both numbers.
video_script.payoff_line: The three products are now compared.

final_answer.spoken: eighteen, two and zero point two

maths_rules: 2.25 × 8: 225 × 8 = 1800, digits after the point 2 + 0 = 2, so 18.00 = 18; 18 is greater than 2.25 and 8
0.25 × 8: 25 × 8 = 200, digits after the point 2 + 0 = 2, so 2.00 = 2; 2 is greater than 0.25 and less than 8
0.25 × 0.8: 25 × 8 = 200, digits after the point 2 + 1 = 3, so 0.200 = 0.2; 0.2 is less than 0.25 and 0.8
size check: 2 × 8 = 16, a quarter of 8 is 2, and 1 × 0.25 = 0.25 with 0.8 a little less than 1
the slip: a product is not always bigger than both numbers
video_script.design: One idea: a number below one takes a part of the other number, so the product is smaller than it. Assumes the digit rule. Wrong idea: a product is always bigger than both numbers. The three products stay all video; the values and the comparison appear only on the answer beat.
